Boutique Nature Resorts in India

Brand Guidelines

Vol. 01 · 2026 · Pench & Tadoba
01The Idea

One flower, many forests

A single mahua flower repeats to become a larger bloom — the way mahua trees gather to become the vann.

The emblem holds the whole brand: one flower for one guest, one lodge, one tree — repeated until it becomes a forest. Everything we design should feel the same way: simple elements, gathered with care.

02Mission · Vision · Philosophy

Why Mahua exists

Our Vision

To be India's most loved boutique nature resorts — living proof that the surest way to protect a forest is to help people fall in love with it.

Our Mission

To build small, warm, earthen lodges at the gates of India's great tiger reserves — run by local hands, rooted in luxury, sustainability and adventure — so every guest leaves as a friend of the wild.

Our Philosophy

The mahua tree feeds the forest and the village alike, asking nothing back. Take gently, give back more.

We believe luxury is the absence of hurry — a lantern instead of a floodlight, a naturalist instead of an itinerary, attention instead of entertainment. The forest sets the pace; our job is simply to keep the lanterns lit.

Brand keywords — the words we return to
EarthenUnhurriedWildRooted Lantern-litLocalCraftedQuiet luxury Safari-firstSustainableWarmIntimate
03The Logo

One mark, treated gently

The logo is always reproduced from master artwork — the name is never re-typeset. Use the full-colour mark on light grounds and the lightened wordmark variant on dark grounds and photography.

xxxx

Clear space — keep a margin of x (the height of the flower's centre) on all sides. Minimum width: 96 px on screen, 28 mm in print.

04Logo Misuse

Never, please

05Colour

Drawn from the flower

The core palette is sampled directly from the emblem. The extended palette carries this design direction — grounds, text and one accent.

07Photography

Shot at the lodge, lit by the lodge

Our imagery comes from our own forests, our own drives and our own lanterns. Four families of pictures, one temperature of light.

The lantern hour

Dusk and after — flame, filament and firelight only.

The forest

Wildlife photographed on our own drives — never stock, never watermarked.

Life at the lodge

People mid-moment — candid, unposed, never looking at the camera.

Details

The small things guests remember — clay, flowers, shrines, hands.
Always
  • Natural or lantern light — golden, warm, believable.
  • Our own wildlife — from drives out of Pench and Tadoba.
  • Texture — mud walls, clay, kilim, canopy.
Never
  • Stock imagery or watermarked photographs.
  • Flash-lit interiors or cold colour grades.
  • Posed groups smiling at the camera.
08Voice

How Mahua speaks

Crisp. Warm. Unhurried.
We say

"The jeep idles before first light. Chai comes with it."

We don't say

"Experience world-class luxury amidst pristine nature at our premium eco-resort!"

We say

"No promises on tigers. Good odds, better guides."

We don't say

"Guaranteed sightings of majestic wildlife await you."
